clue.text: Assortment of types seen in church

definitions.meaning: in printing, a complete set of type in one style and size
the basin holding water for baptism stands in a church

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one word: the printer's set of type, and the baptismal basin in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard dictionary senses: a typeface set in one size, and the stone basin used at christenings.

clue.text: Number on the, bill indicates where the rest may have been taken

definitions.text: where the rest may have been taken

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of the other comes first

parts.note: four is a number
a bill is a printed notice stuck up, a poster

explanation.surface: A figure printed on a bill points to where some remainder was taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' means sleep, not remainder: the definition describes a bed with a post at each corner.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a grand bed with corner posts, a place where someone may have slept.

clue.text: Poke, though not with a pig in it .

definitions.text: Poke, though not with a pig in it .

parts.words: Poke, though not with a pig in it
parts.note: a poke is also an old word for a bag, as in buying a pig in a poke; here the other sense, a prod, is meant

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'a pig in a poke' (something bought unseen, in a bag) tempts you to read poke as a sack; the clue says it is not that sense, so it is a jab.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle push with the elbow is a poke or prod.

clue.text: Piano part I rewrite for unexpected appearance

indicators.note: the clue asks for these letters to be written out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A musician is told to rewrite their piano part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewrite' rearranges PIANO PART I, all ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost or vision is something that appears suddenly and startlingly.

clue.text: Dislike parking on top of here

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
to dislike bitterly is to resent

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes the parking situation on top of everything else here.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in attendance at a place means being right here, as in a roll call reply.

clue.text: Object to leader

explanation.walkthrough: A 'leader' in British newspapers is the editorial, also called a leading article.
explanation.definitionFit: An item or thing is called this, and so is a newspaper editorial piece.

clue.text: Claim a rivet's clamping the Japanese porcelain

indicators.note: the words clamp the answer between them, holding it inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: Someone asserts that a rivet holds a piece of Japanese china together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clamping' signals letters held within: claIM A RIvet's.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a style of brightly decorated porcelain made in Japan, named after its export port.

clue.text: Antrim turns out Russian fighter coming from abroad

indicators.note: the letters are turned out and rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft

explanation.surface: In the Northern Irish county, a Russian jet appears from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges ANTRIM plus MIG; Antrim is a county in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler who has arrived from another country is foreign-born, newly arrived from overseas.

clue.text: Begin to drop off a point - .or not, say?

parts.note: to nod is to start falling asleep, as in nodding off
E is the compass point east

explanation.surface: Someone starts to doze off at a certain point, or perhaps does not.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on sound: 'or not, say' is heard as 'a knot, say', and a botanical joint or knot in a stem is this word.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot or swelling, as on a plant stem, is called this; 'say' marks the definition as heard.

clue.text: Even more brazen undergarment with the bottom cut out

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the final letter, which is removed

parts.note: a brassiere is a woman's undergarment, a bra

explanation.surface: A risqué undergarment designed with its lower part cut away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the bottom cut out' drops the final E of BRASSIERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassy means bold and shameless, so the comparative is more shameless still.

clue.text: Endured having a ducking?

definitions.meaning: a ducking means going under water, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer and it reads 'went under', which is what someone being ducked did.
explanation.definitionFit: To have gone through an ordeal is to have suffered it; split, the word also says something went beneath the water.

clue.text: Directed to give a half back

indicators.note: back says the word for half is read from right to left

parts.note: demi- is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pass half back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns only the word for half, so it follows A reversed; demi- is the prefix in demigod.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointed or steered at a target, as a gun is pointed.

clue.text: Sees they're equal

definitions.meaning: people of the same rank or standing

explanation.walkthrough: One word as a verb (looks hard) and as a plural noun (equals).
explanation.definitionFit: To look closely is a form of seeing, and one's equals are one's fellows in rank.

clue.text: Impressive marks — chins get wagging!

indicators.note: wagging chins move about, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Gossips get their chins wagging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wagging' rearranges CHINS GET.
explanation.definitionFit: Prints made by engraving are marks impressed into a plate, a pun on impressive.

clue.text: Make the worker pay he's the foreman

definitions.meaning: split in two, the answer reads as charge the hand, bill the labourer
a supervisor of a group of workers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' is a worker; charge a hand is to make a worker pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor in charge of a gang of workers, below a foreman in some uses, is so named.

clue.text: In opening up fish, find, otter's dung

indicators.note: the fish is opened up so another piece can go inside it

parts.note: a sprat is a small sea fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gutting a fish, someone finds an otter's droppings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening up' says the fish is split open to take the two-letter word inside; a sprat is a small herring-like fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the hunter's term for the droppings left by an otter.

clue.text: Satirical representation of National Front supporter?

indicators.note: the letters are represented again in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A satirical cartoon depicting a far-right party member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation of' rearranges SATIRICAL. The National Front is a British far-right party.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of a far-right party is typically a person holding racist views; the question mark marks this as an example.

clue.text: I strike, lightly in biblical letter for a grave summing-up

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Eph. is short for Ephesians, an epistle in the New Testament
to tap is to hit gently

explanation.surface: Someone taps on a biblical letter to make a solemn point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the pronoun and the light strike inside the abbreviation for the Epistle to the Ephesians; 'grave' puns on the tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: An inscription on a tombstone sums up a life; grave puns on the burial place.

clue.text: Overwhelm at home with a French fruit

parts.note: in means at home
un is French for a
the date is a fruit of the palm

explanation.surface: Someone at home is overwhelmed by a French fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood or swamp something is to overwhelm it.

clue.text: Turns on again

parts.note: turns are stage acts; acts that come back on stage after the show demands more

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns' looks like a verb but is a noun for performances, and 'on again' means back on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeat performances demanded by an audience are acts brought on again.

clue.text: Cocktail for a fellow traveller

definitions.meaning: a mixed drink of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice
a small carriage fixed to a motorcycle carries a passenger

explanation.walkthrough: A drink of brandy, Cointreau and lemon, and a motorcycle's passenger car.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a classic brandy drink, and also the passenger pod attached to a motorbike.

clue.text: Rates unchanged — unhurried progress

annotationWithheld.why: Rates unchanged — unhurried progress (7): the only parse splits 'unchanged' so the one word gives UN and also its 'changed' indicates the anagram of RATES+UN, a word doing two jobs that the check refuses

clue.text: Girl has admirer in a Russian cloak

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name
a fan is an admirer

explanation.surface: A girl's admirer is wrapped in a Russian cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a long sleeveless dress or pinafore worn as Russian national costume.

clue.text: Register, and clear out!

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to sign in and then get lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges AND CLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of dates and events is kept as a record or schedule, a register.

clue.text: The sort of salt needed for this course.

definitions.text: The sort of salt needed for this course.

parts.words: The sort of salt needed for this course
parts.note: a bitter salt used as a purge, sharing its name with a racecourse

explanation.walkthrough: The salt is the laxative magnesium sulphate; the course is a racecourse in Surrey, England, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: The town in Surrey gives its name to both the purgative salts and the Derby racecourse.

clue.text: Profound needs must be modified

indicators.note: modified means changed, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Deep needs have to be adjusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be modified' rearranges NEEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep or thick, as in impenetrably difficult or heavy, is the sense shared.

clue.text: Tend to follow Union's direction

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a British trade union
SE is the compass direction south-east

explanation.surface: Workers tend to follow the union's line.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after a patient is to care for or tend them.

clue.text: Brandy available for, most of the month

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: March is a month of the year

explanation.surface: A brandy is on offer for most of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a spirit distilled from the grape pulp left after wine pressing.

clue.text: Heavenly butter.

parts.note: a butter is something that butts; the ram butts, and a ram is a constellation in the heavens

explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts with the head, like a ram; the ram in the sky is the zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sign of the zodiac is the Ram, an animal that butts, set in the heavens.

clue.text: Tea, if brewed with care, recommended here?

definitions.text: Tea, if brewed with care, recommended here?

indicators.note: brewing mixes things, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A suggestion that carefully made tea is to be had at this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges TEA IF CARE; the whole clue also describes a place to drink tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service restaurant is a place where tea is served.

clue.text: Boats are able to circumnavigate a river, at this point

indicators.note: to go around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: able to means can
the Tamar is a river in south-west England
S is the compass point south

explanation.surface: Boats can sail around a river at this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to circumnavigate' puts the article and the river inside the word for able; the Tamar divides Devon and Cornwall in England, and 'at this' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Twin-hulled sailing vessels are a kind of boat.

clue.text: Act each way

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone acts both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is something done, an action.
